root_cause.text: The br_nd_send function in the bridge subsystem failed to validate Neighbor Discovery option length fields against the buffer bounds and minimum payload size requirements before parsing, allowing malformed packets to cause out-of-bounds memory access.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description notes that a malformed option can make the parser advance beyond the computed option span or use a too-short source LLADDR option payload, which is addressed in the patch by adding the check `i + (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) > ns_olen` to prevent buffer overruns and `(ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) >= sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN` to validate payload size before reading the address.

intent_record.intent_summary: Added bounds validation checks to prevent buffer overflow vulnerabilities when parsing IPv6 Neighbor Discovery options in bridge packet handling
intent_record.what: Added bounds checking in br_nd_send function: (1) Extended the loop condition to verify i + (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) does not exceed ns_olen, (2) Wrapped daddr assignment with a length validation check ensuring the option contains at least sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN bytes
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds memory access when parsing IPv6 Neighbor Discovery options by validating option lengths before dereferencing pointer arithmetic, protecting against malformed packets that could cause buffer overflows or kernel crashes
